subject: Phased Azure private offer — commitment split & cancellation terms
messages:
From: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@novascale.com>

Cc: Daniel Reed <daniel.reed@novascale.com>, aws-marketplace-ops@amazon.com

Subject: Inquiry: Azure private offer — phased commitment / cancellation options

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for last week’s demo. We’re excited about Redwood but our finance team wants flexibility in the commitment shape for an Azure Private Offer. Specifically: 1) a two-stage annual prepay (Year 1 smaller entry commitment, Year 2+ larger ramp), 2) defined term discounts that increase with committed spend, and 3) a clean early-cancellation mechanism with a limited repayment/credit schedule so we’re not over-committing up front.

Can you share whether Azure Private Offers support a phased commitment split and what the standard cancellation/true-up language looks like? Also, any examples of multi-year discount staircases you’ve put on similar deals would help.

We’d like an initial indicative structure and a sketch of legal language to take to Procurement. I can loop in our Marketplace contact if needed.

Thanks,
Aisha Patel
Head of Procurement, NovaScale

Subject: Re: Inquiry: Azure private offer — phased commitment / cancellation options

Aisha —

Appreciate the clear ask. Short answer: yes, Azure Private Offers via the Marketplace can reflect a phased commitment and we commonly model a staged ramp plus an early-termination true-up that protects both parties. Below is an indicative starting point tailored to the sheet you shared:

- Structure (illustrative):
  • Year 1 prepay: 40% of three-year committed spend (entry + onboarding buffer)
  • Year 2: 35% prepay (ramp)
  • Year 3: 25% prepay (finalization)
- Discounting: tiered percent off list that grows with aggregate annualized commit:
  • <$250k/yr: 8%
  • $250k–$750k/yr: 14%
  • >$750k/yr: 20%
- Cancellation / early termination: pro-rated refund based on unused committed months, minus a fixed transition/service fee (example: 15% of remaining committed value). Alternatively, we offer a credit-based approach where remaining prepay converts to service credit usable for 12 months post-termination (preferred by customers that want to preserve budget).

Legal note (high level): we usually propose an amendment that: defines annual committed SKU quantities, maps Marketplace Private Offer SKUs to Redwood invoice lines, includes a 60-day true-up window after each anniversary, and encodes the early-termination repayment schedule or credit conversion option.

I’ve attached a PDF sketch of the private offer with the tiered discounts and the draft amendment language for Azure Marketplace (Redwood_Private_Offer_2027_v3.pdf). Camila — flag any legal/Marketplace concerns. Karthik — I’ll need a short note from Finance on acceptable fee for early termination if they prefer cash refunds vs credits.

If this looks directionally right I can spin a formal private-offer draft and route for Marketplace listing + DocuSign. Would you prefer a cash-based refund or a credit conversion for NovaScale?

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Aisha — thanks for the clear requirements. Quick legal/ops comments:

- Marketplace constraints: Azure supports multi-line Private Offers but each SKU mapping needs to be explicit. That drives the true-up timing (we recommend a single annual true-up per SKU to simplify reconciliations).
- Cancellation mechanics: our standard amendment currently supports both a cash refund with a 15% administrative adjustment or a credit conversion (credit valid for 12 months). For EU customers we usually prefer the credit path to avoid cross-border refund complexity—but we’ll accommodate cash if Procurement requires it.
- Audit & billing: specify the Billing Owner in the PO so Marketplace can tie the offer to NovaScale’s subscription.

I’ve attached a draft amendment with the proposed wording and a sample clause for early termination (Redwood_Azure_PO_Terms_Amendment_draft.docx). Sean — if NovaScale picks credit vs refund, I’ll bake the exact clause and prepare the Azure Private Offer manifest for Marketplace submission.

—Camila
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Inquiry: Azure private offer — phased commitment / cancellation options

Sean / Camila —

Thanks for the quick responses. Procurement prefers the credit conversion option in principle (easier for our AP and reduces FX headaches), but Finance needs clarity on how credits are valued on termination. Two questions for Redwood: 1) if NovaScale terminates after Year 1, what percentage of the remaining prepay converts to credit (example: 85% net of admin fee?), and 2) can credits be used against Dedicated capacity SKUs or only Hosted API invoices?

We’d like an updated table in your draft that shows three termination scenarios (terminate end of Year 1 / Year 2 / Year 3) and the resulting credit balance under the credit-conversion model. Also please include any Marketplace step that NovaScale needs to complete to accept a Private Offer (contact from our Marketplace admin).

If you can send a version with those tables and a routed DocuSign, we can move to internal approvals.

—Daniel
VP Finance, NovaScale

Daniel / Aisha —

Thanks — good, actionable feedback. Attached is a short matrix that shows the credit conversion examples for termination at each anniversary (I’ll highlight the Year 1 example during the exec review):

- Terminate end of Year 1: 85% of remaining unconsumed prepay converts to Redwood credit (12-month expiry)
- Terminate end of Year 2: 90% converts
- Terminate end of Year 3: 100% converts (no refund needed since term completed)

Credits can be applied to both Hosted API and Dedicated SKU invoices under the same Azure Marketplace account, but credits cannot be redeemed for cash per Marketplace policy; I’ll add the exact Marketplace-account acceptance steps to the DocuSign packet.

Next steps: Camila will produce a redline showing the credit clause and the matrix; I’ll generate the Private Offer manifest and we’ll route via DocuSign to NovaScale’s Marketplace admin. Can we aim to have internal approvals on your side by 2027-04-15 so we can start Marketplace onboarding the following week?
